items.title: Sheila Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Middleburgh, New York, May 11, 2002
items.q: Actually my first bass partner, the first time I ever performed it was with Charles Mingus in Toledo. And he said, “Well why don’t you come up and sing with us.” ... And so I did a duo with Charles Mingus.

ctx.x: Was it a conscious thing at that time? I mean sometimes those things — I’ve heard stories about well this saxophone, this bass thing happened simply because the other people didn’t show up.

Oh no mine was like, mine was I loved the bass. And I remember thinking — actually my Blue Note album, I wanted it to be bass and voice but it was a little bit — nobody wanted to take that chance yet. But thanks to George Russell, who got me the Blue Note date, had made it a trio with guitar, Barry Galbraith, the wonderful Barry Galbraith, and so it was pretty similar but not quite. And there were a couple of things I did with bass and Denzil Best on drums. But originally I wanted that to be a bass and voice. But…

items.title: Sheila Jordan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: And I remember the first time I ever sang in a club with bass and voice was with Charles Mingus.

ctx.x: Who were some of the others?

Oh, Sonny came up to the loft. And Monk came up to the loft. Uh, and then I got, as I said, then I met Mingus, and Mingus and Max were the… Well, Max knew me from Detroit as a kid. But those were the two musicians that recommended that I go, recommended that I go to Lennie Tristano. So that‟s how I got to Lennie Tristano. Charlie Mingus took me there. And that‟s how I started studying with Lennie. And by this time, Duke was in and out, you know. His, his disease took over and, uh, I don‟t know. He went and lived…
